OCOchem completed Task 2, demonstrating the target electrochemical performance parameters of 125 mA/cm2 current density at faradaic efficiency (FE) >70% for >120 hours for the 100 cm2 cell. Issues with gas diffusion electrode (GDE) flooding and catalyst activity over time have been resolved by OCO’s significant development in areas of (a) Gen 2 carbon paper-based gas diffusion electrodes and (b) modified electrochemical reactor’s process operating conditions. Thus, the go/no-go milestone for BP2 was met. OCOchem successfully developed, tested, and demonstrated an electrochemical cell at 540 cm2, exceeding the requirements of 300 cm2 as stated in the proposal. We noted the size of the electrochemical cell would be 300 cm2 (30 cm height x 10 cm width). OCO’s large electrochemical cell with a single panel of GDE, 36 cm height x 15 cm width and thus 540 cm2 of electrochemical (geometric) area, was successfully operated with one and optimized to obtain electrochemical performance close to the target parameters. As part of Task 13 and milestone 13.1, very good electrochemical performance @ >300 cm2 size cell was achieved, meeting almost all the target values for all parameters for 87 hours for a 540 cm2 size GDE. The target current density of 125 mA/cm2 and voltage a bit higher at 4.9 V provided an average of 89% FE (greater than 75% target) over 87 hours, after which it dropped below 75% in discontinuous tests. Biological Upconversion At the University of South Florida (USF), a multi-disciplinary team embarked on a pioneering project to develop an efficient bioconversion process for converting formate to ethylene glycol. This ambitious effort aimed to address critical gaps in sustainable chemical production, with significant implications for clean energy and biomanufacturing sectors. The project was motivated by the urgent need to develop sustainable and economically viable methods for chemical synthesis, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and mitigating environmental impact. Ethylene glycol, widely used in antifreeze and polyester production, represents a valuable target for bio-based production strategies.
